title: Causality, confounding and randomized experiments
objective: Tell association from causation, spot confounding factors, and explain why randomized controlled experiments can establish causality.

items: The factor whose effect you want to know.
What is measured on each individual.
Any relation between treatment and outcome.
A difference between groups, other than the treatment, that affects the outcome.
Individuals randomly assigned to treatment or control, then treated identically otherwise.
Researchers only observe who got the treatment; no random assignment.

blocks.md:
- **Correlation ⇒ causation.** An association can come from a confounder.
- **Letting people choose their group.** Self-selection brings confounders back in.
- **Treating groups differently besides the treatment.** Then any difference could be due to that.

blocks.title: Find the confounder
blocks.problem: Towns with more fire trucks at a fire have more damage. Do fire trucks cause damage?

steps.md: The **size of the fire** drives both: big fires get more trucks and do more damage.
steps.title: Look for a third variable

steps.md: No; the association is explained by fire size.
steps.title: Conclusion

steps.md:
```python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(1)
fire_size = np.random.uniform(1, 10, 200)
trucks = np.round(fire_size + np.random.normal(0, 1, 200))
damage = 50 * fire_size + np.random.normal(0, 40, 200)
print("r(trucks, damage):", round(np.corrcoef(trucks, damage)[0, 1], 2))
```

```text
r(trucks, damage): 0.89
```
steps.title: Complete program (illustration)
steps.why: Trucks don't appear in the damage formula at all, yet r is high.

blocks.answer: Fire size is a confounder; trucks don't cause damage.

blocks.title: Design a fair test
blocks.problem: A team wants to know whether a new coating reduces corrosion on 40 steel plates.

steps.md: Randomly split the 40 plates into 20 treatment (coated) and 20 control (uncoated).
steps.title: Randomize
steps.why: Removes confounders such as batch or position.

steps.md: Same environment and test time for all 40 plates.
steps.title: Treat identically

steps.md: Compare average corrosion between the groups.
steps.title: Compare

steps.md:
```python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(40)
plates = np.arange(1, 41)
shuffled = np.random.permutation(plates)
treatment, control = shuffled[:20], shuffled[20:]
print(len(treatment), len(control))
print(sorted(treatment[:5]))
```

```text
20 20
[np.int64(3), np.int64(23), np.int64(25), np.int64(26), np.int64(30)]
```

blocks.title: Solution: Random assignment
blocks.md:
Full program for **Random assignment** (try it yourself first):

```python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(1330)
people = np.arange(1, 13)
shuffled = np.random.permutation(people)
treatment = shuffled[:6]
control = shuffled[6:]
print("treatment:", sorted(treatment))
print("control:", sorted(control))
```

Output:

```text
treatment: [np.int64(3), np.int64(4), np.int64(5), np.int64(7), np.int64(9), np.int64(10)]
control: [np.int64(1), np.int64(2), np.int64(6), np.int64(8), np.int64(11), np.int64(12)]
```
